zh: 他的第一件大事，便是西征。而凡有大征伐，首先要筹划的是兵、饷二事。左宗棠连日深宵不寐，灯下沉思，已写成了一个筹划的概略；此时从书案抽斗中取了出来，要胡雪岩细看。这个节略先谈兵，次筹饷。而谈兵又必因地制宜，西北与东南的地势，完全不同；南方的军队，到了西北，第一不惯食科；第二不耐寒冷。因此，左宗棠在东南转战得力的将领部队，特别是籍贯属于福建、广东两省的，都不能带到西北。带到西北的，只有三千多人，另外他预备派遣原来帮办福建军务，现已出奏保荐帮办陕甘军务的刘典回湖南，召募三千子弟兵，带到西北。这六千多人，左宗棠用来当作亲兵；至于用来作战的大批部队，他打算在本地招募，要与『关中豪杰』共事业。
en: The first great task was the western expedition. Any major campaign began with two questions: troops and funds. For several nights Zuo had remained awake, thinking beneath the lamp, and had written an outline of his plans. He now took it from a drawer and asked Hu to study it. The outline dealt first with troops, then with finance. Military arrangements had to suit local conditions. The terrain of the northwest differed completely from that of the southeast. Southern soldiers would find the food unfamiliar and the cold intolerable. The effective commanders and units with whom Zuo had fought across the southeast, particularly those recruited in Fujian and Guangdong, could therefore not be taken northwest. He intended to bring only three thousand and more men. Liu Dian, formerly assistant director of military affairs in Fujian and now recommended for the corresponding duties in Shaanxi and Gansu, would return to Hunan to recruit another three thousand men and lead them west. These six thousand and more would form Zuo’s personal force. The main fighting army he intended to raise locally, making common cause with the able men of Guanzhong.

zh: 看到这里，胡雪岩不由得失声说道∶『大人，照你老人家的办法，要什么时候才能平得了回乱？』『你这话，我不大懂。』『大人请想，招募成军，不是一朝一夕的事；练成精锐，更是谈何容易？这一来，要花一两年的功夫。』『岂止一两年？』左宗棠说道∶『经营西域，非十年不足以收功。』『十年？』胡雪岩吓一跳，『那得——。』他虽住口不语，左宗棠也知道，说的是要费多少饷？笑笑说道∶『你不要争！我要在西北办屯垦；这是长治久安之计。就象办船厂一样，不能急切图利；可是一旦见效，你就知道我的打算不错了。』『是！』胡雪岩将那份节略搁下，低着头沉思。『你在想什么？』『我想得很远。』胡雪岩答说∶『我也是想到十年八年以后。』『着！』左宗棠拊掌欣然，『你的意思与我不谋而合；我们要好好打算，筹出十年八年的饷米。』胡雪岩暂且不答，捡起节略再看，大致了解了左宗棠在西北用兵的计划。他要练马队；又要造『两轮炮车』；开设『屯田总局』——办屯垦要农具、要种子、要车马、要垫发未收成以前的一切粮食杂用，算起来这笔款子，真正不在少数。『大人，』胡雪岩问道∶『练马队、造炮车、是致胜所必需，朝廷一定会准。办屯垦，朝廷恐怕会看作不急之务吧？』
en: At this point Hu exclaimed, “Your Excellency, if you proceed in this way, when can the Hui rebellion be suppressed?” “I do not quite understand you.” “Consider, sir. Recruiting an army is not the work of a day, and training it into an elite force is harder still. It will take a year or two.” “A year or two? Establishing the Western Regions will require no less than ten years.” “Ten years!” Hu was startled. “That would take—” He stopped, but Zuo knew he meant the cost. Smiling, he said, “Do not be anxious. I intend to establish agricultural colonies in the northwest. That is the way to lasting peace. As with the shipyard, one must not seek an immediate return. Once the results appear, you will see that I have planned correctly.” Hu set the outline down and bent his head in thought. “What are you considering?” “A long way ahead. I too am thinking eight or ten years into the future.” “Exactly!” Zuo clapped his hands in delight. “Our thoughts coincide. We must plan carefully and find provisions and pay for eight or ten years.” Hu did not answer immediately. He picked up the outline and continued reading until he understood the broad scheme. Zuo intended to train cavalry, build two-wheeled gun carriages, and establish a central bureau for agricultural colonies. The colonies would need implements, seed, carts, horses, and advances for all food and incidental expenses until the first harvest. The amount was considerable. “Your Excellency, cavalry and gun carriages are necessary for victory, and the court will certainly approve them. But might it regard the agricultural colonies as a matter that can wait?”

zh: 『这，你就不懂了。』左宗棠说，『朝中到底不少读书人，他们会懂的。』胡雪岩脸一红，却很诚恳地说∶『是！我确是不大懂，请大人教导。』于是左宗棠为胡雪岩约略讲述用兵西域的限制，自秦汉以来，西征皆在春初，及秋而还。因为第一，秋高马肥，敌人先占了优势；其次就是严寒的天气，非关内的士兵所能适应。『就是为了这些不便，汉武帝元朔初年征匈奴，几乎年年打胜仗，而年年要出师，斩草不能除根，成了个无穷之累。』左宗棠一番引经据典以后，转入正题∶『如今平回乱，亦仿佛是这个道理∶选拔两三万能打的队伍，春天出关，尽一夏天追奔逐北，交秋班师，如当年卫霍之所为，我亦办得到。可是，回乱就此算平了吗？』『自然没有平。』胡雪岩了然了，『有道是「野火烧不尽，春风吹又生。」只要花大功夫拿那块地彻底翻一翻，野草自然长不出来了。』『一点不错！你这个譬喻很恰当。』左宗棠欣慰地说，『只要你懂我的意思，我就放心了。你一定会把我所要的东西办妥当。』这顶『高帽子』出于左宗棠之口，弥觉珍贵；然而也极沉重。胡雪岩知道左宗棠的意思是要他负筹饷的主要责任。凝神细想了一会，觉得兹事体大，而且情况复杂，非先问个明白不可。
en: “That is where you do not understand. There are still many men of learning at court. They will understand.” Hu reddened, but spoke sincerely. “Yes, sir. I do not fully understand. Please instruct me.” Zuo outlined the restrictions upon campaigning in the Western Regions. Since the Qin and Han dynasties, armies had gone west in early spring and returned in autumn. When autumn came and the horses were fat, the enemy held the advantage; the severe cold that followed was also beyond the endurance of troops from within the passes. “Because of these difficulties, Emperor Wu of Han won victories almost every year against the Xiongnu in the early Yuanshuo period, yet had to send an army out again every year. The grass was cut, but the roots remained—a burden without end.” After citing precedents, Zuo returned to the present. “The Hui rebellion presents much the same problem. I could choose twenty or thirty thousand good troops, take them beyond the passes in spring, pursue the enemy through the summer, and return in autumn, as Wei Qing and Huo Qubing did. But would that settle the rebellion?” “Naturally not.” Hu understood. “As the verse says, wildfire cannot burn it all away; the spring wind brings it back. Only by thoroughly turning over the ground can the weeds be prevented from returning.” “Precisely! Your comparison is apt.” Zuo was pleased. “If you understand my purpose, I can rest easy. You will obtain what I need.” Praise from Zuo was precious, but it was also a weighty burden. Hu knew that he was being asked to bear the principal responsibility for raising funds. After concentrated thought, he felt that so great and complicated a matter required some definite answers first.

zh: 『大人，将来要练多少营的队伍。』『这很难说，要到了关外看情形再说。』第一个疑问，便成了难题；人数未定，月饷的数目就算不出来。胡雪岩只能约略估计，以五万人算，每人粮饷、被服、武器；以及营帐锅碗等等杂支，在五两银子以内开支，每月就要二十五万两。于是他再问第二问∶『是带六千人出关？』『是的。大概六千五百人。』左宗棠答说，『三千五百人由闽浙两省动手；另外三千人在湖南招募成军以后，直接出关。』『行资呢？每人十两够不够？』『我想，应该够了。』『那就是六万五千两，而且眼前就要。』胡雪岩又问第三问∶『大人预备练多少马队？』
en: “Your Excellency, how many battalions do you intend to train?” “That is difficult to say. I must see the circumstances beyond the passes.” The very first question thus became a difficulty. Without the number of men, monthly expenditure could not be calculated. Hu could only estimate: at fifty thousand men, with pay, food, clothing, weapons, tents, cooking utensils, and other expenses kept within five taels per man, the total would be two hundred and fifty thousand a month. He asked a second question. “You will take six thousand men beyond the passes?” “Yes. About sixty-five hundred. Thirty-five hundred will set out from Fujian and Zhejiang. Another three thousand, once recruited in Hunan, will go directly west.” “What about travelling expenses? Would ten taels a man suffice?” “I think it should.” “That is sixty-five thousand, needed immediately.” Hu asked his third question. “How much cavalry do you propose to train?”

zh: 『马队我还没有带过，营制也不甚了然。只有自初步打算，要练三千马队。』『那就至少要有三千匹马。』胡雪岩说，『买马要到张家口，这笔钱倒是现成的，我可以垫出来。』『怎么？你在张家口有钱？』『是的。』胡雪岩说，『我有十万银子在张家口，原来打算留着办皮货、办药材的，现在只好先挪来买马。』『这倒好。』左宗棠很高兴地说，『既然如此，我立刻就可以派委员去采办了。』『是！大人派定了通知我；我再派人陪着一起去。』胡雪岩又问，『两轮炮车呢？要多少？』『「韩信将兵，多多益善」。塞外辽阔，险精骑驰骋以外，炮车轰击，一举而廓清之，最是扫穴犁庭的利器！』听这一说，胡雪岩觉得心头沉重。因为他也常听说，有那不恤民命的官军，常常使炮口对准村落，乱轰一气。窝藏在其中的盗匪，固然非死即伤或逃；而遭受池鱼之殃的百姓，亦复不少。
en: “I have never commanded cavalry and do not yet know its battalion organization very well. My preliminary intention is three thousand men.” “Then at least three thousand horses will be needed,” Hu said. “They must be bought at Zhangjiakou. That money is available; I can advance it.” “You have money in Zhangjiakou?” “Yes. A hundred thousand taels, originally intended for furs and medicinal materials. I shall have to use it for horses first.” “Excellent.” Zuo was delighted. “Then I can send a purchasing officer at once.” “Let me know whom you appoint, and I shall send someone with him.” Hu continued, “What about the two-wheeled gun carriages? How many?” “Like Han Xin with soldiers, the more the better. Beyond the passes the country is vast. In addition to swift cavalry, guns on carriages can sweep the ground clear at a stroke. There is no better instrument for destroying the enemy’s strongholds.” Hu’s heart grew heavy. He had often heard of government troops who cared nothing for civilian lives, turned their guns upon villages, and bombarded indiscriminately. Bandits hiding there might be killed, wounded, or driven out, but many innocent inhabitants suffered with them.

zh: 左宗棠所部的洋枪洋炮，多由胡雪岩在上海采办；推原论始，便是自己在无形中造了孽，为了胡雪岩的购办杀人利器，胡老太太不知道劝过他多少次；胡雪岩十分孝顺，家务巨细，母命是从，惟独到公事上头，不能不违慈命。好在胡老太太心地亦很明白；知道不是儿子不听话，实在是无可奈何。因此，只有尽力为他弥补『罪过』，平时烧香拜佛，不在话下；夏天施医施药施凉茶，冬天舍棉衣、散米票，其他修桥铺路，恤老怜贫的善举，只要求到她，无不慷慨应诺。但是，尽管好事做了无其数；买鸟雀放生，总抵偿不了人命，所以胡老太太一提起买军火，便会郁郁不乐。胡雪岩此时听左宗棠说得那么起劲，不由得便想起了老母的愁颜；因而默不作声。
en: Most of the Western firearms and artillery in Zuo’s army had been purchased by Hu in Shanghai. Follow the matter back to its origin, and he himself had unknowingly contributed to wrongdoing. His mother had remonstrated with him countless times over his procurement of weapons that killed people. He was a devoted son and obeyed her in every detail of family affairs. Only in public business did he feel unable to follow her wishes. Fortunately, she understood: it was not deliberate disobedience, but a situation from which he saw no escape. She could only do her utmost to make amends for his “sins.” Besides her customary worship, she provided medical treatment, medicines, and cooling tea in summer, padded clothing and rice vouchers in winter. Anyone seeking help to repair bridges or roads, care for the old, or relieve the poor received a generous promise. Yet however many good deeds she performed, buying birds to release could not compensate for human lives. Every mention of arms purchases saddened her. Hearing Zuo speak so enthusiastically now, Hu saw his mother’s troubled face in his mind and remained silent.

zh: 『怎么？』左宗棠当然不解，『你是不是觉得我要造两轮炮车，有困难？』『不是。我是在想，炮车要多少，每辆要多少银子？这笔预算打不出来。』『那是以后的事。眼前只好算一个约数；我想最好能抽个二十万银子造炮车。』『那末办屯田呢？请问大人，要筹多少银子？』『这更难言了。』左宗棠说∶『好在办屯田不是三年五载的事；而且负担总是越来越轻。我想有个五十万银子，前后周转着用，一定够了。』『是的。』胡雪岩心里默算了一会，失声说道∶『这样就不得了！不得了！』『怎么？』『我算给大人听！』胡雪岩屈指数着∶『行资六万。买马连鞍辔之类，算他一百二十两银子一匹，三千匹就是三万六千。造炮车二十万。办屯田先筹一半，二十五万。粮饷以五万人计，每人每月五两，总共就是二十五万，一年三百万。合计三百五十四万，这是头一年要筹的饷。』这一算，左宗棠也楞住了。要筹三百五十四万两的饷，谈何容易？就算先筹一半，也是一百七、八十万，实在不是一笔小数目了。
en: “What is it?” Zuo naturally did not understand. “Do you think building the gun carriages will be difficult?” “No. I am wondering how many will be required and what each will cost. I cannot draw up that budget.” “That comes later. For now, we must allow a rough amount. I should like to set aside two hundred thousand taels.” “And the agricultural colonies? How much must be raised for those?” “Harder still to say. Fortunately, the colonies are not an undertaking of merely three or five years, and their burden will steadily diminish. I think five hundred thousand taels, used as a revolving fund, will certainly suffice.” Hu calculated silently for a moment, then exclaimed, “This is tremendous! Tremendous!” “How so?” “Let me reckon it for you.” He counted on his fingers. “Travelling expenses, sixty thousand. Horses with saddles and bridles, say a hundred and twenty taels each: three thousand horses make thirty-six thousand. Gun carriages, two hundred thousand. Half the agricultural fund to begin with, two hundred and fifty thousand. Pay and provisions for fifty thousand men at five taels per month, two hundred and fifty thousand monthly, or three million a year. Altogether, three million five hundred and forty thousand. That is what must be raised for the first year.” Zuo too was stunned. Raising three million five hundred and forty thousand taels was no easy matter. Even half—one million seven or eight hundred thousand—was a formidable sum.

zh: 『而且我想，西北运输不便，凡事都要往宽处去算。这笔饷非先筹好带去不可！大人，这不比福州到上海，坐海轮两天功夫就可以到，遇有缓急之时，我无论如何接济得上。西北万里之外，冰天雪地之中，那时大人乏粮缺食，呼应不灵，岂不是急死了也没用？』『说得是，说得是！我正就是这个意思。雪岩，这笔饷，非先筹出来不可；筹不足一年，至少也要半年之内不虞匮乏之好。』『只要有了确实可靠的「军饷」，排前补后，我无论如何是要效劳的。』接着，胡雪岩又分析西征军饷，所以绝不能稍有不继的缘故。在别的省份，一时青黄不接，有厘税可以指拨，有钱粮可以划提，或者有关税可以暂时周转，至不济还有邻省可以通融。西北地瘠民贫，无可腾挪，邻省则只有山西可缓急之恃，但亦有限，而且交通不便，现银提解，往往亦须个把月的功夫。所以万一青黄不接，饥卒哗变，必成不可收拾之势。这个看法，亦在左宗棠深思熟虑的预见之中。因而完全同意胡雪岩的主张，应该先筹好分文不短，一天不延的『的饷』；也就是各省应该协解的『甘饷』。谈到这一层上头，左宗棠便很得意于自己的先见了；如果不是撵走了他的『亲家』郭嵩焘，便顶多只有福建、浙江两个地盘，而如今却有富庶的广东在内。要筹的饷，自然先从这三省算起。
en: “And with transport so difficult in the northwest, we must make generous allowances everywhere. The money has to be secured before you take it with you. This is not like Fuzhou and Shanghai, only two days apart by sea, where I can somehow provide assistance in an emergency. Thousands of miles away, amid snow and ice, if you run short of provisions and cannot make yourself heard, what use will frantic anxiety be?” “Exactly. That is precisely my thought. Xueyan, we must raise it beforehand. If not enough for a year, then at least enough to prevent shortage for six months.” “Provided there is a dependable source of military funds, I shall do everything I can to arrange advances and subsequent receipts.” Hu then explained why the western army could never be allowed even a temporary interruption. Elsewhere, a gap could be filled from likin, land revenue, or customs receipts, or at worst by an accommodation with a neighbouring province. The northwest was barren and poor, leaving no room to move money around. Only Shanxi offered a possible neighbouring resource, and that was limited. Communications were difficult; transporting silver might itself take a month. If funds failed and hungry soldiers mutinied, the situation could become irretrievable. Zuo had foreseen this in his own careful deliberations. He fully agreed that they must first secure funds guaranteed to arrive without a tael missing or a day’s delay: the contributions assigned to the various provinces for Gansu. Here he felt pleased with his foresight. Without driving out his relative by marriage, Guo Songtao, he would have had only Fujian and Zhejiang as bases of support. Now wealthy Guangdong was included. Those three provinces must be the starting point.

zh: 三省之中，又必先从福建开始。福建本来每月协济左宗棠带来的浙军军饷四万两；闽海关每月协济一万两。从长毛余孽肃清以来，协浙的四万两，改为协济甘肃；现在自是顺理成章 归左宗棠了。至于海关的一万两，已籴接济船厂经费；此事是他所首创，不能出尔反尔，这一万两只得放弃。其次是浙江。当杨岳斌接任陕甘总督，负西征全责时，曾国藩曾经代为出面筹饷，派定浙江每月协解两万。上年十月间左宗棠带兵到广东，『就食于粤』的计划既已实现，在胡雪岩的侧面催促之下，不得不守减除浙江负担的诺言。在浙江等于每月多了十四万银子；马新贻是很顾大局的人，自请增拨甘饷三万两，每月共讲五万银子。『浙江总算对得起我；马谷山为人亦很漂亮，每月五万银子协饷，实在不能算少了，不过，』左宗棠停了一下说∶『有两笔款子，在浙江本来是要支出的，我拿过来并不增加浙江的负担，你看如何？』『这要看原来是给什么地方？』『一笔是答应支持船厂的造船经费，每月一万两。现在设厂造船，全由福建关税、厘金提拨；这一万两不妨改为甘饷。』这是变相增加福建负担的办法。胡雪岩心里好笑，左宗棠的算盘，有时比市侩还精；但只要不累浙江，他没有不赞成之理。因而点点头说∶『这一层，我想马中丞决不会反对。』
en: Fujian came first. It had been contributing forty thousand taels a month towards Zuo’s Zhejiang troops, with another ten thousand from Fujian Customs. After the Taiping remnants were cleared, the forty thousand had been reassigned to Gansu. It now naturally came under Zuo’s control. The customs contribution, however, had already been allocated to the shipyard. Since that was his own initiative, he could not reverse himself and had to relinquish those ten thousand. Next came Zhejiang. When Yang Yuebin became governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu with responsibility for the western campaign, Zeng Guofan had helped arrange funds and assigned Zhejiang twenty thousand a month. In the tenth month of the previous year, Zuo had brought his army into Guangdong and achieved his plan of feeding it there. Under Hu’s indirect pressure, he had then had to honour his promise to relieve Zhejiang’s burden. That left Zhejiang with an additional hundred and forty thousand a month. Ma Xinyi, mindful of the wider situation, voluntarily increased the Gansu subsidy by thirty thousand, making fifty thousand monthly. “Zhejiang has treated me well,” Zuo said. “Ma Gushan is a fine man. Fifty thousand a month is no small contribution. But”—he paused—“there are two other sums already budgeted in Zhejiang. Taking those would add nothing to its burden. What do you think?” “That depends on their original destination.” “One is the promised shipbuilding contribution, ten thousand a month. The shipyard is now funded entirely from Fujian Customs and likin. Zhejiang’s ten thousand could be redirected to Gansu.” This was an indirect way of increasing Fujian’s burden. Hu found it privately amusing: Zuo’s calculations could be sharper than a petty merchant’s. But so long as Zhejiang did not suffer, he had no reason to object. “I do not think Governor Ma will oppose that.”

zh: 『另一笔协济曾相的马队，也是一万两。照我想，也该归我。雪岩，你想想其中的道理。』『曾相从前自己定过，江苏协济甘饷，每月三万；听说每月解不足。大人是不是想拿浙江的这一万两，划抵江苏应解的甘饷？』『是啊！算起来于曾无损，为什么不能划帐？』就事论事，何得谓之『与曾无损』？胡雪岩本想劝他，犯不上为这一万两银子，惹得曾国藩心中不快。转念又想，若是这样开口一劝，左宗棠又一定大骂曾国藩。正事便无法谈得下去。因而将到口的话又缩了回去。
en: “The other ten thousand supports Lord Zeng’s cavalry. I think that should come to me too. Consider the reason.” “Lord Zeng originally assigned Jiangsu thirty thousand a month for Gansu, but I hear the full sum is never remitted. Do you propose to offset Zhejiang’s ten thousand against what Jiangsu owes?” “Precisely. It costs Zeng nothing, so why should the accounts not be adjusted?” On the merits, how could it be said to cost Zeng nothing? Hu wanted to advise against displeasing him for the sake of ten thousand taels. Then he reflected that any such advice would make Zuo launch another tirade against Zeng, bringing their serious business to a halt. He swallowed the words.

zh: 这下来就要算广东的接济了。广东的甘饷，本来只定一万；造船经费也是一万，仿照浙江的例子协甘，共是两万。左宗棠意思，希望增加一倍，与福建一样，每月四万。『这一定办得到的。』胡雪岩说，『蒋中丞是大人一手提拔，于公于私，都应该尽心。事不宜迟，大人马上就要写信。』『这倒无所谓，反正蒋芗泉不能不买我的面子，现在就可以打入预算之内。』『福建四万、浙江七万、广东四万、另加江海关三万，，目前可收的确数是十八万；一年才两百十六万。差得很多。』『当然还有。户部所议，应该协甘饷的省份，还有七省。江西、湖北、河南三省，等我这次出关路过的时候，当面跟他们接头；江苏、河南、四川、山东四省的甘饷，只有到了陕西再说。我想，通扯计算，一年两百四十万银子，无论如何是有的。』『那，我就替大人先筹一半。』胡雪岩若无其事地说。『一半？』左宗棠怕是自己没有听清楚，特意钉一句∶『一半就是一百二十万银子。』『是，一百二十万。』胡雪岩说∶『我替大人筹好了带走。』『这，』左宗棠竟不知怎么说才好了，『你哪里去筹这么一笔巨数？』『我有办法。当然，这个办法，要大人批准。等我筹划好了，再跟大人面禀。』左宗棠不便再追着问。他虽有些将信将疑，地是信多于疑；再想到胡雪岩所作的承诺，无一不曾实现，也就释然、欣然了。
en: Next came Guangdong. Its existing contribution to Gansu was only ten thousand; another ten thousand was intended for shipbuilding. Following the Zhejiang precedent, both could go to Gansu, making twenty thousand. Zuo hoped to double that to forty thousand, matching Fujian. “That can certainly be done,” Hu said. “Governor Jiang owes his advancement to you and should exert himself for public and personal reasons alike. There is no time to lose; you should write at once.” “That hardly matters. Jiang Xiangquan cannot refuse me. We may include it in the budget now.” “Fujian forty thousand, Zhejiang seventy thousand, Guangdong forty thousand, and Jianghaiguan Customs another thirty thousand. That gives a dependable hundred and eighty thousand a month, only two million one hundred and sixty thousand a year. The gap is still large.” “There are others, of course. The Ministry of Revenue has designated seven further provinces. I shall speak in person to the authorities in Jiangxi, Hubei, and Henan while passing through on my way west. Jiangsu, Henan, Sichuan, and Shandong must wait until I reach Shaanxi. Taking everything together, I think we can certainly count on two million four hundred thousand a year.” “Then I shall raise half of that in advance for you,” Hu said as though it were a casual matter. “Half?” Zuo wondered if he had heard correctly. “Half is one million two hundred thousand taels.” “Yes. I shall have it ready for you to take.” “But—” Zuo scarcely knew what to say. “Where will you find such an enormous sum?” “I have a method. Naturally, it will require your approval. Once I have worked out the arrangements, I shall explain them.” Zuo could not press further. He was doubtful, but more confident than doubtful. Remembering that Hu had fulfilled every promise he had made, he felt reassured and pleased.

zh: 『大人什么时候动身，什么时候出关？』『我想十一月初动身，沿途跟各省督抚谈公事，走得慢些，总要年底才能到京。』『到京？』胡雪岩不解地问，『上谕不是关照，直接出关。』这哪里是上头的意思？无非有些人挟天下以令诸侯。他们怕我进京找麻烦，我偏要去讨他们的厌；动身之前，奏请陛见。想来两宫太后决不致于拦我。『左宗棠停了一下又说∶』至于出关的日期，现在还不能预定。最早也得在明年春天。『』那还有三四个月的功夫。大人出关以前，这一百二十万一定可筹足；至于眼前要用，二、三十万银子，我还调度得动。『』那太好了！雪岩我希望你早早筹划停当，好让我放心。『这又何消左宗棠说得？胡雪岩亦希望早早能够定局。无奈自己心里所打的一个主意，虽有八成把握，到底银子不曾到手。俗语说的『煮熟了鸭子飞掉了』，自是言过其实；但凡事一涉银钱，即有成议，到最后一刻变卦，亦是常有之事。一百二十万两不是个小数目，西征大业成败和左宗棠封爵以后能不能入阁拜相的关键都系于此，关系真个不轻。倘或功败垂成，如何交代？兴念及此，胡雪岩深深失悔，何以会忘却『满饭好吃，满话难说？之戒？如今既不能打退堂鼓，就得全力以赴加紧进行。
en: “When will you leave, sir, and when do you expect to pass beyond the frontier gates?” “I intend to leave early in the eleventh month. I shall travel slowly, discussing affairs with governors and governors-general along the way. I shall probably not reach the capital until the year’s end.” “The capital? Did the edict not direct you to proceed straight to the west?” “That was hardly the intention of Their Majesties. It was certain men using the authority of the realm to command its governors. They fear I shall cause trouble in the capital. I mean to be a nuisance to them. Before leaving, I shall request an audience. I do not believe the two empress dowagers will refuse.” Zuo paused. “As for passing beyond the gates, I cannot fix the date yet. Next spring at the earliest.” “Then we have another three or four months. The million two hundred thousand will be ready before you go. For immediate needs, I can still arrange two or three hundred thousand.” “Excellent! Xueyan, settle it as soon as you can, so that I may rest easy.” Hu needed no such reminder. He too wished to settle the matter quickly. Although he gave his plan an eight-in-ten chance, the silver was not yet in his hands. The proverb about a cooked duck flying away was an exaggeration, but where money was concerned, even an agreed arrangement could change at the last moment. A million two hundred thousand was no trifling sum. The western expedition’s success, and whether Zuo might rise from his noble title to a grand secretaryship, depended upon it. If the plan failed just before completion, how could Hu answer for it? He deeply regretted forgetting the warning: a full bowl of rice is easy to eat, but a sweeping promise is hard to fulfil. Since he could not retreat, he must throw all his strength into carrying it through.
